renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: coverage_curve
  title: Coverage against sequencing effort
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sequencing library: the average coverage of its metagenome that the reads reach (vertical axis) as the sequencing effort grows (horizontal axis, log scale). It answers how much more sequencing a library needs before it describes its community.
    How to read: a curve that flattens near the top has captured most of the community, and extra sequencing adds little. A curve that still climbs steeply is far from covered, and the projected effort in the summary tiles says how much deeper to go. Compare curves of the same habitat only, since diversity sets the slope.
    Lines and annotations: the curves are redrawn from Nonpareil's fitted model (a gamma distribution on the log of the effort) and not from the measured redundancy points, which nf-core does not publish. Nonpareil projects effort for 95 percent coverage by default.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lmrodriguezr/nonpareil/master/utils/Nonpareil/R/Nonpareil.R and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24123672/
  kind: profile
  config:
    log_x: true
    x_title: Sequencing effort (bp)
    y_title: Estimated average coverage
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: library
    x: sequencing_effort
    y: coverage

- component: figure
  title: Coverage curves, static view
  description: |-
    Each line is a sequencing library: the estimated average coverage against the sequencing effort on a log scale. It answers the same question as the interactive curve tile, in a plain figure that can be exported.
    How to read: lines reaching the top at a lower effort belong to simpler communities. A line that ends low means the run stopped well short of covering the community.
    Note: the lines are rebuilt from Nonpareil's fitted model, not from measured points.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lmrodriguezr/nonpareil/master/utils/Nonpareil/R/Nonpareil.R and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24123672/
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sequencing_effort
    y: coverage
    color: library
    log_x: true
    labels:
      sequencing_effort: Sequencing effort (bp)
      coverage: Estimated average coverage
      library: Library

- component: interactive
  title: Library
  description: Filters the tiles to one or more sequencing libraries.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: library

- component: table
  title: Curve points
  description: |-
    Each row is one point of a library's rebuilt coverage curve, with the sequencing effort, the estimated coverage, the effort actually sequenced and the effort projected for 95 percent coverage. It answers the exact values behind the curves.
    How to read: filter by library and compare its observed effort with its projected effort to see how far the run is from the target.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lmrodriguezr/nonpareil/master/utils/Nonpareil/R/Nonpareil.R

- component: card
  title: Average coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of the metagenome that the reads already reach, with the lowest and highest library. It answers how completely the libraries describe their communities.
    How to read: a value near 1 means more sequencing would add few new sequences. A low value means a large part of the community is still unseen, so check the effort multiple card for how much deeper to go.
    Lines and annotations: the marker is 95 percent coverage, the default coverage for which Nonpareil projects the effort needed. It is the target of the method and not a pass or fail rule.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lmrodriguezr/nonpareil/master/utils/Nonpareil/R/Nonpareil.R
  column: coverage
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.95
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: average coverage, against the 95 percent target

- component: card
  title: Sequence diversity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median Nonpareil diversity index (Nd) of the libraries, and the box shows their spread. It answers how diverse the sequenced communities are.
    How to read: the index is on a log scale, so a higher value means a more diverse community that needs more sequencing to cover. Compare libraries of the same habitat.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29657970/
  column: diversity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Effort still needed
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of how many times deeper a library must be sequenced to reach 95 percent coverage, with the smallest and largest multiple. It answers how far the run is from the projected target.
    How to read: a multiple close to 1 means the library is nearly there. A large multiple marks a diverse community that the current depth only samples.
    Lines and annotations: the target is the 95 percent coverage Nonpareil projects by default, and the multiple is its projected effort divided by the effort sequenced.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lmrodriguezr/nonpareil/master/utils/Nonpareil/R/Nonpareil.R
  column: effort_multiple
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: median, with the shallowest and the deepest need

- component: card
  title: Samples and libraries
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples with a Nonpareil fit, and the strip counts their sequencing libraries. It answers how many libraries the coverage figures are drawn from.
    How to read: more libraries than samples means a sample was sequenced in several runs, each with its own curve.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: samples, with the libraries counted

- component: figure
  title: Coverage against diversity
  description: |-
    Each point is a sequencing library: its diversity index on the horizontal axis, its estimated coverage on the vertical axis, coloured by sample and sized by the effort still needed. It answers whether the libraries that are least covered are the most diverse.
    How to read: points at the lower right are diverse communities that are far from covered, the ones to sequence deeper. Large points need the most extra effort.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median estimated coverage of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Nonpareil.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29657970/
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: diversity
    y: coverage
    color: sample
    size: effort_multiple
    labels:
      diversity: Nonpareil diversity (Nd)
      coverage: Estimated average coverage
      sample: Sample
      effort_multiple: Effort multiple
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: coverage
    label: Median coverage

- component: interactive
  title: Coverage range
  description: Filters the tiles to libraries whose estimated coverage falls inside the chosen range.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: coverage

- component: table
  title: Coverage and diversity table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sequencing library with its fitted model: coverage, sequencing effort, projected effort for 95 percent coverage, the effort multiple and the diversity index. It answers the exact numbers behind each card.
    How to read: sort by effort multiple to find the libraries that need the most extra sequencing.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29657970/
